faq.title: Why does Google Dialer blast 'This call is now being recorded' to both parties?
faq.description: Google mandates the automated two-party consent announcement to protect itself from wiretapping and privacy lawsuits across jurisdictions with strict two-party recording consent laws (such as California and Germany). Even in jurisdictions where one-party consent is legally valid (such as India and many US states), Google's default Phone app enforces the loud announcement globally.

faq.title: Is call recording legal in India without informing the other party?
faq.description: Under Indian jurisprudence and precedents established by the Supreme Court of India, India operates effectively under a 'one-party consent' framework for personal conversations. Recording a telephone call to which you are an active participant is legally permissible and admissible as documentary evidence under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, provided the audio is authentic and unedited.

faq.title: Why do third-party call recorders on the Play Store only record my voice and not the other person?
faq.description: Beginning with Android 10 and finalized in Android 13, Google removed the internal telephony audio recording API (`VOICE_CALL` audio source) for third-party apps to prevent spyware abuse. Standard Play Store apps only have access to your microphone, which captures your voice clearly but can only record the other person's voice faintly through acoustic speaker bleed unless an Accessibility/Shizuku bridge is utilized.

html:
The Frustration of the Mandatory Warning Announcement

You answer an important business call from a client agreeing to project deadlines, receive a harassing call from an aggressive debt collector violating banking regulations, or conduct an in-depth journalistic interview. You tap the 'Record' button on your Android smartphone's screen.

Instantly, a mechanical, booming voice announces over the earpiece and speaker: 'THIS CALL IS NOW BEING RECORDED.' The other party immediately stops speaking, becomes defensive, or abruptly hangs up the phone. What should have been an indispensable tool for business documentation and legal self-defense is rendered completely useless.

This loud announcement is not a hardware limitation; it is an intentional policy enforced by Google's Phone (Dialer) app, which now ships as the default dialer across Google Pixel, Xiaomi, Motorola, OnePlus, Realme, and Nothing smartphones. However, millions of professionals require reliable, discrete call recording for legitimate record-keeping. This comprehensive technical guide details the verified methods to record telephone calls cleanly on modern Android without the warning announcement.

The Legal Context: Understanding One-Party vs Two-Party Consent

Before implementing these solutions, understand the legal landscape governing telephone recording:

  • One-Party Consent Jurisdictions (Including India): In India and 35 US states, recording a conversation is legally permitted as long as at least one participant in the conversation consents. Because you are a participant and consent to your own recording, you are legally entitled to record the conversation without notifying the other party. Tape recordings have been repeatedly upheld as valid electronic evidence under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act.
  • Two-Party / All-Party Consent Jurisdictions: In states like California, Florida, and countries like the UK and Germany, all parties on a phone call must be explicitly informed that recording is occurring. Always verify your regional legal statutes when recording business or legal discussions.

Method 1: The TTSLexx Silence Exploit (Works on Google Dialer)

If your smartphone uses the default Google Phone app, you can eliminate the audible announcement using a clever architectural exploit involving Android's Text-to-Speech (TTS) engine:

How the TTSLexx Exploit Works:

Google Dialer does not play a static MP3 file for the announcement; it uses Android's active Text-to-Speech engine to synthesize the sentence 'This call is now being recorded' right before the recording buffer opens. By substituting Google's Speech Services with an open-source, blank speech synthesizer named TTSLexx, the announcement is rendered into complete silence!

Step-by-Step Configuration:

  1. Install TTSLexx from the Google Play Store (it is a free, zero-permission, open-source utility).
  2. Open your phone's Settings > System > Languages & input > Text-to-speech output (on Samsung: General management > Text-to-speech).
  3. Tap on Preferred engine.
  4. Change the preferred engine from Speech Recognition and Synthesis from Google to TTSLexx.
  5. Tap OK on the system warning modal.
  6. Critical Step — Flushing the Google Dialer Cache:
    • Long-press the Phone (Google Dialer) app icon on your home screen > tap App info.
    • Tap Storage and cache.
    • Tap Clear Data / Clear Storage. (Do not worry: your contacts, call history, and favorites are stored in a separate system database and will NOT be erased).
  7. Make a test phone call and tap Record. You will notice that the announcement is 100% silent! The audio buffer opens immediately without alerting either party.

Method 2: Replacing Google Dialer with Native Manufacturer Dialers

Hardware manufacturers like Samsung, OnePlus, and OPPO maintain their own proprietary telephony dialers that feature clean, built-in, unannounced call recording:

1. Samsung Galaxy (One UI Native Call Recording)

Samsung smartphones sold across India and many international regions include the gold standard of call recording built directly into the native One UI Phone app:

  1. Open the native Phone app on your Samsung device.
  2. Tap the three dots in the upper-right corner > tap Settings.
  3. Tap on Record calls.
  4. Toggle ON: Auto record calls. You can configure it to automatically record: All calls, Calls with unsaved numbers, or Calls with specific contacts.
  5. Samsung's native recorder records both sides with crystal-clear hardware quality and never plays an announcement.

2. OnePlus, Realme, and OPPO (ODialer App)

For devices running OxygenOS, ColorOS, or Realme UI, ColorOS maintainers released their authentic legacy dialer on Google Play under the name ODialer:

  1. Install ODialer from the Google Play Store.
  2. Set ODialer as your Default phone app in Settings > Apps > Default apps.
  3. Open ODialer > Settings > Call recording > Auto-record all calls.
  4. ODialer communicates directly with ColorOS hardware audio drivers, recording both parties cleanly with zero warning prompts.

Method 3: Cube ACR with Shizuku / App Connector Bridge

If you need to record VoIP audio across WhatsApp calls, Telegram voice calls, Skype, and cellular voice simultaneously, Cube ACR is the most versatile third-party tool available:

Solving Android 13/14/15 Audio Sandboxing:

Because Google removed raw audio capture APIs for third-party apps, Cube ACR requires installing the Cube ACR App Connector (downloadable directly from Cube's official website). By granting the App Connector permission via Shizuku (wireless ADB) or Accessibility Services, Cube ACR bridges the kernel audio stream, capturing both incoming and outgoing channels with pristine clarity.

Hardware Audio Routing: Why Android 14/15 Blocks Simple Recording

Many users wonder why an app that recorded phone calls effortlessly on an Android 8 device fails to capture the caller's voice on Android 14 or 15. The explanation lies in modern hardware security partitioning:

  • The Modern Cellular Audio Path: Modern baseband modems (Qualcomm Snapdragon X-series and MediaTek 5G UltraSave) route incoming cellular voice packets directly to the hardware digital signal processor (DSP) without exposing the unencrypted digital PCM stream to Android's general user-space memory.
  • The Deprecation of VOICE_CALL Audio Source: In Android 10, Google deprecated the MediaRecorder.AudioSource.VOICE_CALL enum constant. When an unprivileged app calls this API today, the operating system kernel immediately throws an IllegalArgumentException security error.
  • How Shizuku Restores Audio Capture: By leveraging Shizuku, advanced recording utilities like Cube ACR obtain elevated ADB system privileges. Shizuku injects a lightweight helper hook into the Android audio framework, capturing the mixed hardware speaker buffer before it is routed to your ear.

Configuring Automated Recording Rules for Financial Security

To maximize legal and personal protection without cluttering your phone with thousands of recorded calls, configure automated recording rules:

  1. Open your dialer's recording settings (Samsung Phone, ODialer, or Cube ACR).
  2. Change the recording mode from 'All Calls' to 'Calls with Unknown Numbers'.
  3. Every phone call from an unsaved number (such as delivery agents, unknown business entities, customer support, or potential scam callers) is automatically recorded and archived in high-fidelity Opus format.
  4. Calls from verified family members, personal friends, and doctors are bypassed, respecting personal privacy and saving valuable flash storage space.
  5. Set up an automated cleanup rule to auto-purge recordings older than 90 days unless you manually tag them as 'Starred / Important'.

Legal Evidence Standards: Section 65B Compliance & Metadata Verification

If you are recording telephone calls for business contracts, tenancy agreements, or legal disputes, ensuring the recordings are admissible in a court of law requires strict cryptographic hygiene:

  • Preserving Original Audio Containers: Never edit, trim, or re-encode your call recording files. Converting a raw recording from WAV/AMR into an MP3 file alters the file's hash, inviting accusations of audio tampering by opposing legal counsel.
  • Section 65B Electronic Evidence Certificates: Under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act (and equivalent electronic records statutes globally), you must accompany digital recordings with a signed affidavit affirming that the recording device was operating properly, that the file was preserved without alteration, and detailing the date, time, and caller identity.
  • Cloud Backup with Client-Side Encryption: Store your primary call recording archive in an encrypted local vault or zero-knowledge cloud drive (such as Proton Drive or Cryptomator). Never upload sensitive legal call recordings to unencrypted public cloud storage links.

Preventing Battery Optimization from Killing Call Recorders

Modern Android battery managers aggressively kill background apps. If you notice that your call recorder fails to record incoming calls after your phone has been asleep for an hour, configure these two settings:

  1. Go to Settings > Apps > [Your Recorder / ODialer / Cube ACR] > Battery.
  2. Change the setting from Optimized to Unrestricted.
  3. In your phone's Recent Apps multitasking switcher, long-press the app window and select Lock this app. This prevents the OS memory manager from purging the recording daemon during RAM cleanups.

Preventative Architecture & Companion Recommendations

Establishing clear, dependable call recording safeguards your professional agreements and provides vital evidentiary security.
